explanation: A voltage tripler multiplies a lower AC voltage to the many kilovolts needed by the CRT anode.
choice_notes: 5 V comes straight from the transformer and rectifier.

question: The heading flash is a momentary intensification of the sweep line on the PPI presentation. Its function is to:
choices: Alert the operator when a target is within range.
Alert the operator when shallow water is near.
Inform the operator of the dead-ahead position on the PPI scope.
Inform the operator when the antenna is pointed to the rear of the ship.
explanation: The heading flash brightens the sweep each time the antenna points dead ahead, showing the ship's heading on the PPI.
choice_notes: It marks the bow, not the stern.

question: The major advantage of digitally processing a RADAR signal is:
choices: Digital readouts appear on the RADAR display.
Rectangular display geometry is far easier to read on the CRT.
explanation: Digital processing (sweep correlation and averaging) pulls weak target echoes out of noise and clutter.

question: In order to ensure that a practical filter is able to remove undesired components from the output of an analog-to-digital converter, the sampling frequency should be:
choices: The same as the lowest component of the analog frequency.
Two times the highest component of the analog frequency.
Greater than two times the highest component of the sampled frequency.
The same as the highest component of the sampled frequency.
explanation: Nyquist: sample at more than twice the highest signal frequency, so the anti-alias filter can practically remove unwanted components.

question: Bearing resolution is:
choices: The ability to distinguish two adjacent targets of equal distance.
The ability to distinguish two targets of different distances.
The ability to distinguish two targets of different elevations.
The ability to distinguish two targets of different size.
explanation: Bearing resolution is the ability to show two targets at the same range but slightly different bearings as separate echoes. It depends on horizontal beamwidth.
choice_notes: That's RANGE resolution (set by pulse width).

question: The output of an RC integrator, when driven by a square wave with a period of much less than one time constant is a:
explanation: When the period is much shorter than RC, the capacitor charges and discharges only a little, almost linearly, each half cycle. The output is a small triangle wave.

question: How do you eliminate stationary objects such as trees, buildings, bridges, etc., from the PPI presentation?
choices: Remove the discriminator from the unit.
Use a discriminator as a second detector.
explanation: The pool's answer: using a discriminator (phase-sensitive detector) as the second detector, as in MTI processing, cancels echoes whose phase doesn't change from pulse to pulse, i.e. stationary objects.

question: Slotted waveguide arrays, when fed from one end exhibit:
explanation: A slotted waveguide fed from one end radiates a beam whose angle shifts with frequency (frequency scanning), because the slot phasing depends on wavelength.
choice_notes: It's matched at the terminated far end.
True, but not caused by end-feeding.

question: A typical shipboard RADAR antenna is a:
explanation: Most ship RADAR antennas are slotted waveguide arrays.
choice_notes: Parabolic dishes: older sets and long range.

question: Good bearing resolution largely depends upon:
choices: A narrow antenna beam in the vertical plane.
A narrow antenna beam in the horizontal plane.
explanation: Bearing resolution depends on a narrow horizontal beamwidth, i.e. a long antenna.
choice_notes: The VERTICAL beam is deliberately wide (for ship roll).

question: The center of the transmitted lobe from a slotted waveguide array is:
choices: Several degrees offset from a line perpendicular to the antenna.
Maximum at the right hand end.
Maximum at the left hand end.
explanation: In an end-fed slotted array the main lobe is squinted a few degrees away from the perpendicular. The RADAR compensates for this offset.

question: How does antenna length affect the horizontal beamwidth of the transmitted signal?
choices: The longer the antenna the wider the horizontal beamwidth.
The longer the antenna the narrower the horizontal beamwidth.
The horizontal beamwidth is not affected by the antenna length.
explanation: Beamwidth ≈ 70 λ / length (in degrees), so a longer antenna gives a narrower horizontal beam.

question: What is the most common type of RADAR antenna used aboard commercial maritime vessels?
explanation: The slotted waveguide array is the standard commercial marine RADAR antenna.

question: The VSWR of a microwave transmission line device might be measured using:
choices: A dual directional coupler and a power meter.
A dual directional coupler, a power meter, and a network analyzer.
explanation: A dual directional coupler samples forward and reflected power, measured with a power meter or network analyzer, giving the reflection coefficient and hence VSWR.
choice_notes: A spectrum analyzer measures frequency content, not VSWR.

question: The impedance total (ZO) of a transmission line can be calculated by ZO = √L/C when L and C are known. When a section of transmission line contains 250 microhenries of L and 1000 picofarads of C, its impedance total (ZO) will be:
If long-length transmission lines are not properly shielded and terminated:
choices: The silicon crystals can be damaged.
explanation: Unshielded or mismatched long lines radiate and pick up energy, causing interference to communications receivers.
choice_notes: The TR cell protects the crystals.

question: A certain length of transmission line has a characteristic impedance of 72 ohms. If the line is cut at its center, each half of the transmission line will have a ZO of:
choices: The exact length must be known to determine Zo.
explanation: Characteristic impedance depends on the line's geometry and dielectric, not its length. Each half is still 72 Ω.

question: Standing waves on a transmission line may be an indication that:
choices: All energy is being delivered to the load.
Source and surge impedances are equal to ZO and ZL.
The line is terminated in impedance equal to ZO.
Some of the energy is not absorbed by the load.
explanation: Standing waves come from reflected energy, which means the load isn't absorbing all of it (a mismatch).
choice_notes: That's the matched case (no standing waves).

question: What precautions should be taken with horizontal waveguide runs?
choices: They should be sloped slightly downwards at the elbow and a small drain hole drilled in the elbow.
They should not exceed 10 feet in length.
explanation: Horizontal waveguide runs should slope slightly toward an elbow with a small drain hole, so condensation drains out instead of pooling.

question: The position of the PPI scope sweep must indicate the position of the antenna. The sweep and antenna positions are frequently kept in synchronization by the use of:
explanation: Synchro systems transmit the antenna's angular position to the display so the sweep rotates in step.
choice_notes: Servos drive motors. Synchros send the angle.

question: On a basic synchro system, the angular information is carried on the:
explanation: In a synchro, the rotor is excited with AC and the three stator lines carry voltages whose ratios encode the angle.
choice_notes: Deflection coils are in the display.
The rotor carries the AC excitation.

question: What is the most common type of antenna position indicating device used in modern RADARs?
explanation: Modern RADARs typically use resolvers (or encoders) to report antenna position.
choice_notes: Step motors: not used for indication.

question: Which of the following statements about antenna resolvers is correct?
choices: Most resolvers contain a rotor winding and a delta stator winding.
Resolvers consist of a two rotor windings and two stator windings that are 90 degrees apart.
The basic resolver contains a rotor winding and two stator windings that are 90 degrees apart.
Resolvers consist of a "Y" connected rotor winding and a delta connected stator winding.
explanation: A resolver has a rotor winding and two stator windings at 90°, which output sine and cosine of the rotor angle.
choice_notes: A delta stator is a synchro.
That's a differential resolver, not the basic one.

question: An antenna synchro transmitter is composed of the following:
choices: Three rotor and two stator windings.
Two rotor and three stator windings.
Three rotor and three stator windings.
A single rotor and 3 stator windings.
explanation: The pool's answer: a synchro transmitter has a rotor (two leads) and three stator windings.

question: RADAR antenna direction must be sent to the display in all ARPAs or RADAR systems. How is this accomplished?
explanation: Antenna bearing can be sent by synchros, resolvers or optical encoders. Any of the above.

question: Waveguides can be constructed from:
explanation: Waveguides are made of good conductors: brass, aluminium or copper (often silver-plated inside).

question: A microwave transmission line constructed of a center conductor suspended between parallel conductive ground planes is called:
explanation: Stripline: a centre strip conductor sandwiched in dielectric between two ground planes. (Microstrip has one ground plane.)
choice_notes: Microstrip: a conductor above ONE ground plane.
Coax: a center conductor in a round shield.
Waveguide: a hollow pipe, no center conductor.

question: Waveguide theory is based upon:
choices: The movement of an electromagnetic field.
explanation: A waveguide guides an electromagnetic field (wave) bouncing between its walls. It isn't current flow in a wire.

question: A waveguide is used at RADAR microwave frequencies because:
choices: It is easier to install than other feedline types.
It is more rugged than other feedline types.
It is less expensive than other feedline types.
It has lower transmission losses than other feedline types.
explanation: At microwave frequencies, waveguide has much lower loss than coax.

question: Waveguide theory is based on the principals of:
choices: Skin effect and use of ¼ wave stubs.
explanation: Waveguide theory can be pictured as a bundle of quarter-wave shorted stubs (which look like open circuits) supporting a centre conductor that has been removed. Skin effect confines currents to the inner surface.

question: How is the signal removed from a waveguide or magnetron?
choices: With a thin wire called a T-hook.
With a thin wire called a J-Hook.
explanation: A small wire probe (J-hook) inserted into the waveguide or magnetron couples the energy out.
choice_notes: Coax is used at S-band in some sets, but J-hook is the answer.
A flange joins sections. It doesn't extract the signal.

question: A rotary joint is used to:
choices: Couple two waveguides together at right angles.
Act as a switch between two waveguide runs.
Connect a stationary waveguide to the antenna array.
Maintain pressurization at the end of the waveguide.
explanation: A rotary joint lets the stationary waveguide run feed the rotating antenna.

question: Resistive losses in a waveguide are very small because:
choices: The inner surface of the waveguide is large.
The inner surface of the waveguide is small.
The waveguide does not require a ground connection.
The heat remains in the waveguide and cannot dissipate.
explanation: Currents in a waveguide flow over its large inner surface area, so resistance (and loss) is low compared with coax's thin centre conductor.

question: A right-angle bend in an X-band waveguide must have a radius greater than:
explanation: X-band waveguide bends need a radius larger than about 2 inches (about 2 wavelengths) to avoid reflections.

question: To insert RF energy into or extract RF energy from a waveguide, which of the following would not be used?
explanation: Energy enters or leaves a waveguide via a probe (E-field), a loop (H-field) or an aperture (slot or window). Coupling capacitance isn't a waveguide method.

question: The following is true concerning waveguides:
choices: Conduction is accomplished by the polarization of electromagnetic and electrostatic fields.
The magnetic field is strongest at the center of the waveguide.
The magnetic field is strongest at the edges of the waveguide.
explanation: In the dominant TE10 mode the electric field peaks at the centre of the broad wall, and the magnetic field is strongest near the edges (narrow walls).
choice_notes: The magnetic field is strongest at the walls.

question: At microwave frequencies, waveguides are used instead of conventional coaxial transmission lines because:
choices: They are smaller and easier to handle.
They are lighter since they have hollow centers.
Moisture is never a problem with them.
explanation: At microwave frequencies coax losses become large. Waveguide carries the power with much less loss.

question: When you examine the RADAR you notice that there is no target video in the center of the CRT. The blank spot gets smaller in diameter as you increase the range scale. What operator front panel control could be misadjusted?
explanation: A blank spot in the centre that shrinks on longer ranges means close-range echoes are being suppressed, typically the STC (sea clutter) control set too high.

question: Range rings on the PPI indicator are oval in shape. Which circuit would you suspect is faulty?
explanation: Oval range rings mean the X and Y sweep amplitudes aren't equal, pointing to the sweep generation circuits.
choice_notes: Timing faults change spacing, not shape.

question: What would be the most likely defective area when there is no target video in the center of the CRT and the blank spot gets smaller in diameter as your range scale is increased?
explanation: A blank centre can mean the TR cell is recovering too slowly after each pulse (de-ionizing late), keeping the receiver muted for the first part of each sweep.
choice_notes: A mistuned LO weakens ALL echoes.

question: While the vessel is docked the presentation of the pier is distorted near the center of the PPI with the pier appearing to bend in a concave fashion. This is a primary indication of what?
choices: The centering magnets at the CRT neck need adjusting.
The waveguide compensation delay line needs adjusting.
explanation: The waveguide compensation delay line corrects for the delay in long waveguide runs. If it's misadjusted, near-range objects are displaced and a straight pier looks bent near the centre.
choice_notes: The deflection coils affect the whole picture.

question: In a RADAR using digital video processing, a bright, wide ring appears at a fixed distance from the center of the display on all digital ranges. The transmitter is operating normally. What receiver circuit would you suspect is causing the problem?
choices: Video storage RAM or shift register.
explanation: A fixed ring at the same distance on all digital ranges points to a stuck bit in the video storage (RAM or shift register).
choice_notes: The VRM is a thin, adjustable ring.
Range rings are thin, multiple and scale with range.

question: The raster scan RADAR display has missing video in a rectangular block on the screen. Where is the most likely problem area?
explanation: A rectangular block of missing video on a raster display maps to a block of memory addresses, so suspect a memory failure.
choice_notes: Sweep faults give lines or collapse.

question: A circuit card in a RADAR system has just been replaced with a spare card. You notice the voltage level at point E in Fig. 8F12 is negative 4.75 volts when the inputs are all at 5 volts. The problem is:
choices: The 100 K resistor has been mistakenly replaced with a 50 K resistor.
The op amp is at the rail voltage.
The 50 K resistor has been mistakenly replaced with a 25 K resistor.
explanation: Fig. 8F12: with 5 V on all inputs, E should be −10k x 5 x (1/200k + 1/100k + 1/50k + 1/25k) = −3.75 V. −4.75 V is 1 V more, exactly what doubling the 50k input's current would add (5/25k − 5/50k = 0.1 mA x 10k = 1 V).

question: A defective crystal in the AFC section will cause:
choices: Bright flashing pie sections on the PPI.
Vertical spikes that constantly move across the screen.
explanation: A failed AFC crystal lets the local oscillator drift, so the picture fades in and out in bright flashing pie-shaped sectors as tuning wanders.

question: The RADAR display has sectors of solid video (spoking). What would be the first thing to check?
explanation: Sectors (spokes) of solid video are usually interference from another ship's RADAR nearby. Check that first.
choice_notes: Antenna data faults give smearing or rotation.

question: In the circuit contained in Fig. 8F12, there are 5 volts present at points B and C, and there are zero volts present at points A and D. What is the voltage at point E?
If the TR tube malfunctions:
explanation: If the TR tube fails to fire, the full transmitter pulse reaches the mixer crystal and can destroy the receiver front end.
choice_notes: The transmitter is protected by the ATR.
The klystron isn't in the signal path.

question: The indicated distance from your own vessel to a lighthouse is found to be in error. What circuit would you suspect?
explanation: Wrong range readings to a known object point to the range-measuring circuitry: the range ring (marker) oscillator calibration.

question: Silicon crystals are used in RADAR mixer and detector stages. Using an ohmmeter, how might a crystal be checked to determine if it is functional?
choices: Its resistance should be the same in both directions.
Its resistance should be low in one direction and high in the opposite direction.
Its resistance cannot be checked with a dc ohmmeter because the crystal acts as a rectifier.
It would be more appropriate to use a VTVM and measure the voltage drop across the crystal.
explanation: A good crystal behaves like a diode: low resistance one way and high the other. Equal readings mean it's shorted or open.
choice_notes: That's a short or an open.
Rectification is exactly what an ohmmeter can show.

question: In a RADAR unit, if the crystal mixer becomes defective, replace the:
choices: The crystal and the ATR tube.
The crystal and the TR tube.
explanation: A burned-out mixer crystal usually means the TR tube let transmitter energy through, so replace both or the new crystal will fail too.
choice_notes: A failed TR probably caused the crystal failure.
The ATR doesn't protect the crystal.

question: An increase in magnetron current that coincides with a decrease in power output is an indication of what?
explanation: If the magnet weakens, electrons aren't curved enough. They go straight to the anode, so current rises while microwave output falls.
choice_notes: High SWR causes moding and arcing.

question: It is reported that the RADAR is not receiving small targets. The most likely causes are:
choices: Magnetron, IF amplifier, or receiver tuning.
Crystals, local oscillator tuning, or power supply.
Fuse blown, IF amp, or video processor.
explanation: Missing small targets means weak echoes or poor sensitivity: low magnetron output, low IF gain, or receiver mistuning.

question: A high magnetron current indicates a/an:
explanation: High magnetron current indicates a weak or defective magnetic field.
choice_notes: High SWR causes moding and arcing.

question: Low or no mixer current could be caused by:
explanation: Mixer current comes from LO drive into the crystal. It drops if the LO is off frequency or weak, if the TR cell blocks it, or if the mixer diode degrades. All of the above.

question: If the magnetron is allowed to operate without the magnetic field in place:
choices: Its output will be somewhat distorted.
It will quickly destroy itself from excessive current flow.
explanation: Without the magnetic field, the electrons rush straight from cathode to anode. The magnetron draws huge current and destroys itself.

question: Targets displayed on the RADAR display are not on the same bearing as their visual bearing. What should you first suspect?
choices: A bad reed relay in the antenna pedestal.
One phase of the yoke assembly is open.
explanation: If RADAR bearings don't match visual bearings, suspect the antenna position information (heading alignment, synchro or resolver).

question: Loss of distant targets during and immediately after wet weather indicates:
choices: A leak in waveguide or rotary joint.
Dirt or soot on the rotary joint.
High humidity in the transmitter causing power supply loading.
explanation: Water entering a leaking waveguide or rotary joint absorbs and reflects energy, reducing range until it dries.
choice_notes: That would be immediate and natural, not a fault.

question: In a marine RADAR set, a high VSWR is indicated at the magnetron output. The waveguide and rotary joint appear to be functioning properly. What component may be malfunctioning?
explanation: With the waveguide and rotary joint OK, high VSWR points to the antenna itself, e.g. a failed termination load at the end of the slotted array.
choice_notes: Possible, but the question points to the far end.

question: On a vessel with two RADARs, one has a different range indication on a specific target than the other. How would you determine which RADAR is incorrect?
choices: Check the sweep and timing circuits of both indicators for correct readings.
Triangulate target using the GPS and visual bearings.
Use the average of the two indications and adjust both for that amount.
explanation: Range accuracy depends on each indicator's sweep and timing. Check both against known references to find the one in error.

question: An increase in the deflection on the magnetron current meter could likely be caused by:
choices: Insufficient pulse amplitude from the modulator.
Too high a B1 level on the magnetron.
A decrease of the magnetic field strength.
A lower duty cycle, as from 0.0003 to 0.0002.
explanation: A weaker magnetic field lets more electrons reach the anode, so magnetron current rises.
choice_notes: A lower duty cycle = less current.

question: A thick layer of rust and corrosion on the surface of the parabolic dish will have what effect?
choices: Scatter and absorption of RADAR waves.
Decrease in performance, especially for weak targets.
Slightly out of focus PPI scope.
explanation: Corrosion on a reflector surface scatters and absorbs some energy, reducing gain. Weak targets suffer first.

question: The echo box is used for:
choices: Testing the wavelength of the incoming echo signal.
Testing and tuning of the RADAR unit by providing artificial targets.
explanation: An echo box (resonant cavity) rings after each transmitted pulse, giving an artificial target to test and tune overall performance.

question: What should be done to the interior surface of a waveguide in order to minimize signal loss?
choices: Paint it with nonconductive paint to prevent rust.
Keep it as clean as possible.
Fill it with a high-grade electrical oil.
explanation: A clean, smooth inner surface keeps resistive and scattering losses low. Dirt and corrosion raise loss.
choice_notes: Nitrogen pressurization keeps moisture out, but cleanliness is the answer.

question: Which of the following is the most useful instrument for RADAR servicing?
explanation: Most RADAR waveforms (triggers, modulator pulses, video, sweeps) are best examined with an oscilloscope.

question: A non-magnetic screwdriver should always be used when replacing what component?
explanation: A magnetron has a powerful permanent magnet. A steel screwdriver can be pulled in, damage it, or weaken the magnet, so use non-magnetic tools.

question: What kind of display would indicate water in the waveguide?
choices: Large circular rings near the center.
explanation: Water in the waveguide reflects energy, producing extra rings near the centre of the display.
choice_notes: Loss of rings = a marker fault.
Wide targets = beamwidth or pulse width.

question: Why is coaxial cable often used for S-band installations instead of a waveguide?
choices: Losses can be kept reasonable at S-band frequencies and the installation cost is lower.
A waveguide will not support the power density required for modern S-band RADAR transmitters.
S-band waveguide flanges show too much leakage and are unsafe for use near personnel.
Dimensions for S-band waveguide do not permit a rugged enough installation for use by ships at sea.
explanation: At S-band (3 GHz), good coax has tolerable loss and is much cheaper and easier to install than the large S-band waveguide.

question: RADAR interference to a communications receiver is eliminated by:
choices: Not operating other devices when RADAR is in use.
Properly grounding, bonding, and shielding all units.
Using a high pass filter on the power line.
explanation: Proper grounding, bonding and shielding keep RADAR pulses from radiating or conducting into communications receivers.

question: Why should long horizontal runs of waveguide be avoided?
choices: They must be insulated to prevent electric shock.
To prevent damage from shipboard personnel.
To minimize reception of horizontally polarized returns.
explanation: Condensation collects in horizontal waveguide runs, causing loss and corrosion. Avoid them or slope them to drain.

question: Long horizontal sections of waveguides are not desirable because:
choices: Moisture can accumulate in the waveguide.
The waveguide can sag, causing loss of signal.
The polarization of the signal might shift.
explanation: Moisture accumulates in long horizontal waveguide sections.

question: In a RADAR system, waveguides should be installed:
choices: As straight as possible to reduce distortion.
At 90 degree angles to improve resonance.
As long as possible for system flexibility.
explanation: Bends and twists add reflections and loss, so waveguide should run as straight as practical.

question: What is the most important factor to consider in locating the antenna?
choices: Maximum height for best long range operation.
The antenna is in a location that is not shadowed by other structures.
explanation: The antenna must have a clear view. Masts and structures that shadow the beam create blind sectors.

question: Choose the most correct statement with respect to component damage from electrostatic discharge:
choices: ESD damage occurs primarily in passive components which are easily identified and replaced.
ESD damage occurs primarily in active components which are easily identified and replaced.
The technician will feel a small static shock and recognize that ESD damage has occurred to the circuit.
ESD damage may cause immediate circuit failures, but may also cause failures much later at times when the RADAR set is critically needed.
explanation: ESD often causes latent damage: a weakened junction may work now and fail later, possibly when the RADAR is critically needed.

question: Before testing a RADAR transmitter, it would be a good idea to:
choices: Make sure no one is on the deck.
Make sure the magnetron’s magnetic field is far away from the magnetron.
Make sure there are no explosives or flammable cargo being loaded.
Make sure the Coast Guard has been notified.
explanation: RADAR emissions near explosive or flammable cargo operations can ignite vapours. Make sure none is being handled before transmitting.

question: While making repairs or adjustments to RADAR units:
choices: Discharge all high-voltage capacitors to ground.
explanation: RADAR supplies and PFNs store lethal charges. Discharge all high-voltage capacitors to ground before working.

question: While removing a CRT from its operating casing, it is a good idea to:
choices: Test the second anode with your fingertip.
Set it down on a hard surface.
explanation: A CRT is a high-vacuum glass bulb that can implode. Wear gloves and goggles when handling it.

question: If a CRT is dropped:
choices: Most likely nothing will happen because they are built with durability in mind.
It might go out of calibration.
It might implode, causing damage to workers and equipment.
explanation: A dropped CRT may implode, throwing glass fragments at high speed.

question: Prior to removing, servicing or making measurements on any solid state circuit boards from the RADAR set, the operator should ensure that:
choices: The proper work surfaces and ESD grounding straps are in place to prevent damage to the boards from electrostatic discharge.
The waveguide is detached from the antenna to prevent radiation.
The magnetic field is present to prevent over-current damage or overheating from occurring in the magnetron.
Only non-conductive tools and devices are used.
explanation: Use an ESD-safe work surface and grounded wrist straps to protect sensitive solid-state boards.
